meta.description: Calculate your debt-to-income ratio with neutral band explanations.

header.title: Debt-to-income (DTI) calculator
header.intro: Divide your monthly debt payments by your gross (before-tax) monthly income to see your DTI and where it falls in commonly used ranges.

demoBanner.strong: Educational estimate — not a lending decision.
demoBanner.body: Bands are general reference points, not approval criteria for any lender.

monthlyIncome.label: Monthly gross income
monthlyIncome.hint: Before taxes. Include salary, self-employment taxable income, alimony/support received, etc.

monthlyDebts.label: Monthly debt payments
monthlyDebts.hint: Rent or mortgage (incl. taxes/insurance/HOA), car, student, personal loans, card minimums, support payments. Exclude utilities, food, insurance premiums.

cardBalance.label: Credit card balances not included above (est.)
cardBalance.hint: Optional. We add an estimated minimum payment for these balances.

results.invalidMessage: Fix the highlighted fields to see an estimate.
results.heading: Your estimated DTI

good.label: 35% or less — generally considered manageable
good.body: Many lenders look for a DTI in this range. A lower DTI can leave more room in your budget.

fair.label: 36% to 43% — may need work
fair.body: Some lenders may still work with this range, though options or terms can be more limited.

high.label: 44% or more — high
high.body: Your budget may be stretched. Reducing payments or increasing income can lower DTI.

results.summaryMessage: DTI is one factor lenders may consider; it is not a credit score and does not guarantee approval or terms. Bands are general reference points only.

cta.label: Explore ways to lower DTI
cta.note: Placeholder CTA — demo only, not a live application or offer.

footer.note: Achieve-styled demo for product exploration only. Not financial, tax, legal, or insurance advice.
